column3: “His work is perfect” renders “perfect is His work”; “without injustice” renders “there is no injustice.”
The Hebrew of this line is difficult; NASB’s “because of their defect” renders “their blemish,” and the meaning is uncertain.
“who has bought you” renders a verb that may mean “created” or “acquired.”
“all generations” renders “generation and generation”; “elders” renders “old ones.”
“the sons of man” renders “the children of humankind”; “the sons of Israel” follows the Hebrew, where some ancient witnesses read “sons of God.”
“the Lord’s portion” uses a lowercase “Lord” for “Yahweh.”
NASB uses “He … them” in the last two lines, where the Hebrew has “it … it.”
“the finest of the wheat” renders “the fat of the kidneys of wheat”; “the breed of Bashan” renders “sons of Bashan.”
NASB puts “You are grown fat, thick, and sleek” between dashes; “scorned” renders “treated with contempt.”
“dread” renders a rare verb, also read as “know”; the meaning is uncertain.
“what is not God” renders “not a god”; “idols” renders “vanities.”
“is kindled” and “burns” render Hebrew perfect forms; “yield” renders “produce.”
“I would have said” renders “I said”; “men” renders “humankind.”
